patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a prominent search field in the header area; the desktop sketch explicitly includes a search icon/button at the right edge of the input, and the mobile sketch shows a large centered search bar near the top.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: The search field should accept text input and submit a query, likely via Enter key and search button/icon. It may also support focus styling and possibly clearing/active-state behavior implied by the prominent treatment.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not clearly show autocomplete or live suggestions, so only submit/search behavior is certain; live results would be speculative.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The search bar is a user-input form control in both mobile and desktop layouts, with an explicit submit affordance on desktop and an implied submit action on mobile.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: At minimum, the form should handle empty or malformed submissions gracefully, preserve focus behavior, and submit entered queries. Validation here is likely lightweight, mainly around empty input handling.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit error states are drawn, so full validation messaging is not clearly required beyond basic search form handling.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Near the top of both sketches there is a horizontal row of short labeled items beneath the search area, with one item visually emphasized/boxed in the desktop sketch and a segmented navigation-like row in the mobile sketch. This strongly suggests content-category tabs.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Selecting a tab should switch the active category/view and visually mark the selected tab. The associated content may reload or swap below the header without leaving the page, depending on implementation.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear whether these are true client-side tabs or simple navigation links to separate pages; the boxed active item suggests tab-like state, but content-panel swapping is inferred.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches contain multiple image thumbnails and larger hero images, which in article/gallery layouts commonly imply tap/click-to-enlarge behavior. The repeated framed image placeholders suggest interactive media viewing.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Clicking or tapping an image should likely open a larger overlay/lightbox view, especially for gallery items and the main article image. Focus should move into the overlay and return to the trigger on close.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not explicitly depict an overlay state, so enlargement could alternatively navigate to a dedicated image page rather than open a modal.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show long article content followed by multiple image-card groupings and additional content blocks, implying expandable or progressively revealed related media/content sections in a content-heavy page.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If the gallery or related content is truncated initially, a load-more interaction could reveal additional items without full page navigation.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit button or pagination control is drawn, so this is only a plausible enhancement, not a clearly required interaction.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a relatively simple content/article experience with a strong search-first header, category switching near the top, and image-heavy article sections that likely need click/tap enlargement behavior. Cross-viewport differences are mostly layout-related rather than interaction-related: desktop makes the search submit affordance and active top-category state more explicit, while mobile compresses the same functions into a stacked layout. No clear evidence appears for hamburger navigation, dropdowns, accordions, sticky elements, live counters, or infinite scrolling.
